# target_ct bytes from memory dump at 0x402060
target_ct = bytes([0xe7, 0xab, 0x72, 0x33, 0xc0, 0x55, 0xf0, 0x70, 
                   0x17, 0xa2, 0x25, 0xc1, 0x5a, 0xc3, 0x99, 0x38,
                   0xa3, 0x40, 0xe9, 0x9b, 0x10, 0x89, 0x01, 0x5f,
                   0xaf, 0xfe, 0x7d])

# Algorithm:
# edx starts at 0xffffffa1 (signed -95, but treated as low byte = 0xa1 = 161)
# For each char:
#   input_char XOR edx_low_byte == target_ct[i]
#   then edx += input_char
# 
# To reverse: input_char = target_ct[i] XOR edx_low_byte
# then edx += input_char

edx = 0xffffffa1 & 0xffffffff  # 32-bit value
result = []

for i in range(27):
    # Get low byte of edx for XOR
    edx_low_byte = edx & 0xff
    # input_char XOR edx_low_byte == target_ct[i]
    # So input_char = target_ct[i] XOR edx_low_byte
    input_char = target_ct[i] ^ edx_low_byte
    result.append(input_char)
    # Update edx: edx += input_char (32-bit arithmetic)
    edx = (edx + input_char) & 0xffffffff

solution = bytes(result)
print(f"Solution: {solution}")
print(f"Length: {len(solution)}")
